about:
Competition Specialties Inc., operating as Competition Specialties, LLC, is headquartered in Auburn, Washington. The company was established in 1966 and marks 60 years in business as of 2026. Ownership details beyond the LLC structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm functions as a wholesale distributor of automotive parts and accessories, carrying over 145 major product lines that span offroad, exterior, interior, towing, and adventure categories. It operates four strategically located West Coast warehouses, achieving average fill rates above 94 percent. Services include drop-ship fulfillment, secure real-time internet ordering, a 200-plus-page full-color retail catalog, and a knowledgeable phone sales team. The company also maintains a private-label house brand, CSI Private Label, and runs a Performance Corner Marketing Program for its customers.

Competition Specialties serves jobbers and retailers in the automotive aftermarket, including powersports and adventure-accessory segments. Its customer base consists primarily of wholesale distributors (jobbers) who attend the company's annual jobber-only trade show. Brands carried include Warn, Factor 55, Thule, Rockslide, Streamlight, and Ram Mounts.

The company emphasizes aggressive pricing and unmatched service as its core differentiators, supported by high fill rates, multi-warehouse logistics, and dedicated marketing support for its dealer network.

name: Complete Medical Supply Inc
old_description: Our knowledgable sales representatives look forward to helping you!
about:
Complete Medical Supply Inc is based in Suffern, New York, and was founded in 1988. The company operates as a health product manufacturer, importer, and master wholesaler. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures its own Blue Jay™ brand of healthcare products and offers a catalog of over 14,000 medical, homecare, ergonomic, and healthcare items. Its manufacturing arm, Complete Medical Supplies Manufacturing Group, produces the Blue Jay line. Services include drop shipping with no minimum orders, custom assembly of college student kits for physical therapy, occupational therapy, nursing, and medical programs, a 24/7 online ordering platform called Complete-Connect™, custom flyer creation, and datafeed integration for resellers. Local truck delivery is available in its service area.

Customers include medical-surgical facilities, homecare providers, ergonomic product retailers, and healthcare distributors. The company also serves college and university programs, providing custom PT/OT/nurse/medical student kits. Both professionals (end users) and resellers can open accounts.

Complete Medical Supply emphasizes cost reduction through offshore sourcing solutions, no-minimum-order drop shipping, and digital tools like Complete-Connect™ for round-the-clock ordering and account management. The custom flyer and datafeed programs aim to help resellers market products more effectively.

about:
Composite Fabrics of America LLC operates from Hiddenite, North Carolina, as a wholly owned subsidiary of Schneider Mills, one of the oldest and most advanced weaving mills in the United States. The company leverages that heritage to produce carbon fiber and composite reinforcements for demanding applications.

The firm specializes in producing industry-standard and custom reinforcing materials for aerospace composite part fabrication and repair. Its textile engineering team develops custom reinforcing products to meet design-specific requirements, reduce waste, or add aesthetic appeal, and offers a "Bill and Hold" service to buffer customers against price and availability fluctuations.

Primary markets include aerospace, automotive, infrastructure, and athletics. Customers range from aerospace fabricators and repair stations to automotive and industrial designers seeking collaborative development of innovative components.

The company cites its AS9100 Rev D certification, the legacy of Schneider Mills' weaving expertise, and its in-house textile engineering capability as key differentiators that enable high-quality, tailored composite fabrics.

about:
Computer Cable Connection, Inc. (CCC) is based in Omaha, Nebraska, and was established in 1986 as a full-service BICSI and RCDD network cable design and installation firm. The company serves private, state, and federal institutions across the United States. No founder names or ownership details are publicly disclosed.

CCC provides a range of communications infrastructure services including structured cabling, fiber optic installation and repair, fusion splicing, testing, termination and certification, and custom cable assemblies built to specified length, color, and termination. The firm also designs and installs rack and cabinet layouts, cable management, UPS/PDU systems, distributed antenna systems (DAS), sound masking, audio/visual solutions, intercom and paging, and medical equipment installations. With over 30 years of experience, the company reports more than 30,000 completed projects and a network of 870-plus appointed contractors.

The client base spans commercial, government, and healthcare sectors, with explicit mention of medical equipment installation, federal and state institutions, and private enterprises. Projects have been executed in thousands of facilities nationwide.

CCC emphasizes a client-satisfaction process that moves from discovery and solution design through installation and switchover support. Technicians are trained and certified to manufacturer specifications and BICSI standards, and the company highlights its on-time delivery record and partnership approach with customers and suppliers.

about:
Conner Industries operates from Lewisburg, Tennessee, where it was founded in 1986. The company has grown to 14 locations across the United States, providing industrial packaging and wood products to manufacturers nationwide.

The company manufactures custom pallets, crates, and integrated packaging solutions using materials such as southern yellow pine, hardwood, corrugate, foam, and plastics. Its service portfolio includes packaging consultation and design, unit load testing through independent labs, warehousing, third-party logistics, vendor-managed inventory, kitting, assembly, co-locating, repackaging, and just-in-sequence delivery. Conner focuses on wholesale and bulk orders, leveraging its multi-site network for redundancy and rapid response.

Its customer base spans energy, oil and gas, automotive, aerospace and defense, chemical and plastics, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, consumer products, HVAC and appliance, heavy industrial, agricultural, and logistics sectors. The company also supplies export-compliant, heat-treated lumber for international shipments.

Conner differentiates itself by offering multi-material design not limited to a single substrate, outsourcing validation testing to avoid conflicts of interest, and emphasizing sustainable, carbon-negative wood packaging. Its wholesale-only model aims to keep pricing competitive while maintaining multiple redundancies to ensure supply continuity.

name: Consolidated Metco Inc
old_description: Driving the industry forward with transformative solutions since 1964
about:
Consolidated Metco Inc., operating as ConMet, was founded in 1964 as part of Portland Freightliner, a subsidiary of Consolidated Freightways. The company began in Clackamas, Oregon, and now bases its corporate headquarters in Vancouver, Washington. In 1999, Amsted Industries acquired ConMet through its purchase of Varlen Corp., and the business remains a division of that diversified global manufacturer. From its start, ConMet focused on wheel-end components, aiming to make critical truck and trailer parts lighter, higher quality, and more efficient.

Today ConMet designs and manufactures wheel-end assemblies (including its flagship PreSet® and PreSet Plus® hubs), brake drums, structural plastic components, permanent-mold aluminum castings, and aerodynamic devices such as TruckWings. Its processes span CNC machining, plastic assembly, foundry and machining operations, aluminum die casting, heat treating, and advanced molding. The company runs 13 global manufacturing locations across North America, Mexico, China, and Europe, and reports more than 60 million hubs produced and over 3 billion products shipped annually, with 18 million-plus vehicles on the road using ConMet parts.

ConMet serves the commercial vehicle industry, supplying original equipment manufacturers, commercial fleets, and the heavy-duty aftermarket. Its customer base includes European OEMs, North American truck and trailer builders, and fleet maintenance operations. Through Amsted Industries, the company also touches the railroad, automotive, construction, and building markets.

ConMet emphasizes collaboration through a full design–development–testing–validation cycle, advanced automation, rigorous quality assurance, and sustainable manufacturing practices such as high-efficiency furnaces, heat-treat optimization, extensive recycling, and reduced energy consumption. The company traces its purpose to solving the industry’s most pressing problems with smarter, safer, and more sustainable solutions.

name: Consolidated Telcom
old_description: Consolidated is the premier provider of telecommunication services in Southwestern North Dakota since 1961. Customer service is our main priority, from customer service representatives, internet and service support, to our technicians in the field. You, our customer, are our number one priority, 24/7/365.
about:
Consolidated Telcom, based in Dickinson, North Dakota, traces its roots to January 2, 1961, when the Bowman-Slope Rural Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation and the Dunn Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation merged to form the Consolidated Telephone Cooperative. The cooperative is owned by its members—customers who use its services—and operates as a not-for-profit entity serving southwestern North Dakota.

The cooperative delivers voice, video, and data services across 19 rural communities and the Dickinson area, operating a 100% fiber-to-the-home network in its cooperative exchanges and a hybrid fiber-coax system in Dickinson. Its wholly owned subsidiaries provide competitive local exchange (CLEC) service, internet access, and cable television. Consolidated has invested millions of dollars in network infrastructure since its founding.

Customers include residential subscribers in communities such as Amidon, Dodge, Dunn Center, and Bowman; businesses in Dickinson, Belfield, and Gladstone; and institutions like Dickinson State University, which was the cooperative’s first CLEC customer. The cooperative was originally formed by farmers, ranchers, and local residents who banded together to obtain telephone service that commercial providers deemed unprofitable to offer.

The member-owned structure means a locally elected board of directors governs operations, and revenues above operating expenses are returned to members as capital credits based on usage. Consolidated’s motto, “Reach the World from Here,” reflects its mission to bring urban-level telecommunications to rural areas at comparable cost, driven by a commitment to honesty, integrity, and community service rather than profit.
